page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an arm64 instance type built around the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration, avoiding hyperthreading concurrency contention. The core configuration is supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning is configured in a memory-optimized 1:8 ratio, providing 64 GB of system RAM corresponding to 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration includes standard AES instructions, while x86-specific vector extensions and hypervisor flags are absent.

Benchmark analysis reflects notable strengths in memory throughput and single-threaded operations. The instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score alongside 200.21 GB/sec of uncached large-block read bandwidth. Single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression, scored in the upper quartile. Text processing demonstrated strong throughput. However, workloads relying on specialized instruction sets show distinct performance limitations: PassMark encryption testing ranked in the lower 25 percent, and prompt processing for medium 7B language models delivered weak throughput due to the absence of advanced matrix or vector extensions.

The c4a-highmem-8 does not include bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all data persistence relies entirely on network-attached storage volumes. GPU acceleration is also absent. From a resource-density perspective, the machine provides high RAM-per-core density, allowing organizations to avoid overpaying for unnecessary compute cores when running memory-heavy tasks. Given these performance and resource boundaries, the server fits in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, memory-intensive relational and analytical databases, text parsing pipelines, and general backend application serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an arm64 instance configured with a memory-optimized footprint. Powered by 8 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, the server avoids hyperthreading contention with single-threaded cores. It couples 64 GB of system RAM at an 8 GB per core ratio with an 80 MB L3 cache, yielding top-tier memory benchmark scores and 200.21 GB/sec uncached large-block read bandwidth. Single-threaded compression and text processing show strong performance, while cryptographic testing and language model prompt processing reflect lower relative throughput. The configuration provides no integrated local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block volumes for storage. This architectural profile fits in-memory caching, databases, ETL pipelines, and high-memory web services.
